title: Frontend: Billing Counter
businessContext: Build and verify the core behavior behind Billing Counter. This independently authored exercise has a bounded, explicit contract. Injected clock, network, random, or worker models are identified in the contract; they do not claim production service guarantees.
problemStatement: Export App. Quantity is integer 0..100, Unit is nonnegative integer cents, Discount is integer percent 0..100. Return {subtotal,discount,total}, rounding the discount once to nearest cent. Invalid fields show Invalid bill. Render controlled labelled inputs with these exact names: Quantity, Unit, Discount. A Calculate submit button computes the result. Render JSON.stringify(result) in [data-testid="result"]. Validation failure clears result and shows the documented message in [data-testid="error"].
constraints: Export default App. Only react and react/jsx-runtime imports are supported. The DOM contract and supplied props define the exercise.
Preserve identity, ordering, boundary behavior, and error messages stated in the contract. Passing fixtures verifies this contract, not every production concern.
candidateTasks: Implement the documented behavior without hard-coding fixture answers.
Run the full suite, investigate boundary failures, and explain the follow-up variation.
hints: Write down the state or algorithmic invariant, and trace the smallest boundary case before coding.
Store quantities and item IDs, derive line totals, and calculate the bill from authoritative unit amounts.
alternativeApproaches: Add tax-inclusive pricing and define whether rounding occurs per line or for the whole invoice.
commonMistakes: Ignoring contract boundaries such as: Zero quantity; quantity limit; percentage rounding.
Treating a local deterministic model as proof of durable storage, authorization, distributed coordination, or physical-world guarantees.
